title: Chiefs back in business as star QBs go down - five things from NFL week two
description: Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs look back to their best but Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels suffer serious injuries. Here's what you need to know from week two in the NFL.
fullText:
After a feast of points in week one, defences hit back in week two of the NFL.

The Chicago Bears came crashing back down to earth after a flying start - and they suffered one of the two worrying injuries to two of the league's top young quarterbacks.

The Kansas City Chiefs were back doing what they do best but the Baltimore Ravens were surprisingly beaten, while two games were settled in overtime and one decided with just nine seconds on the clock.

Here's our pick from Sunday's week two action.

Allen stars as Bills open new stadium in style

The Chicago Bears scored 59 points last week but just three this time in an ugly 9-3 home loss to the Vikings, as Minnesota won their seventh straight game at Soldier Field.

The 56-point drop-off is the second most in NFL history as the Bears saw two touchdowns lost with a dropped catch and a fumble, had a field goal blocked but worst of all lost their star quarterback Caleb Williams.

The first pick of the 2024 draft was carried off the field in the fourth quarter looking in serious pain, but initial reports are that his hamstring injury may not be as serious as first feared.

Jayden Daniels was the second pick of that 2024 draft behind Williams and he left Washington's defeat at Dallas with a serious injury to the same elbow he dislocated last season.

Daniels, who seems certain to be out for some time, would still have struggled to keep up with Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott who threw four touchdowns in their 37-20 victory.

Prescott surpassed Tony Romo's team record of 248 touchdown passes by taking his tally to 249.

The Kansas City Chiefs gave another ominous sign that they were back in business with a 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Winning tight games was a hallmark of the Patrick Mahomes dynasty during three recent Super Bowl wins, so there was a familiar feeling when Harrison Butker kicked the winning field goal right at the death.

Mahomes threw three touchdowns and his 382 passing yards was his most for three years. Travis Kelce had 101 yards and a touchdown and summer signing Kenneth Walker had another huge game.

The Super Bowl MVP had 178 total yards and was crucial in overtime to help overcome a strong challenge from Daniel Jones and the Colts - who may have lost their first two games but look to have plenty to build on.

The Green Bay Packers also triumphed in overtime by erasing a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter against the New York Jets to win 20-17 - and snap a six-game losing streak.

Super Bowl champions Seattle look the real deal again after beating the Arizona Cardinals 31-7 for a 12th straight win.

Drew Lock showed he is no ordinary back-up quarterback with three touchdown passes to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, including an 82 yarder that is the longest of the talented receiver's career.

The Seahawks lost Walker to the Chiefs but have retained a remarkable 17 of 22 starters and 44 of their 53-man roster from last season's title win.

That consistency should see them go close again, but they'll face a rejuvenated San Francisco 49ers in their division, who are also 2-0 after beating the Miami Dolphins 35-15.

Showing no signs of jet leg from their victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, the Niners scored touchdowns on their first five possessions to blow Miami away - Christian McCaffrey scored twice, George Kittle also found the end zone and Brock Purdy accounted for three scores.

With the 49ers having their defensive stars back from injury Kyle Shanahan's squad look the total package once again.

The Cincinnati Bengals also look more well rounded this season after winning a 20-6 battle in Houston, thanks to an early touchdown of the season contender catch from Ja'Marr Chase.

We expect fireworks from Chase and Joe Burrow, but having a defence capable of keeping CJ Stroud out of the end zone, and sacking him four times in a road game is the biggest reason for optimism among Bengals fans.

The Philadelphia Eagles were on the ropes against the Tennessee Titans until Jalen Hurts threw the winning touchdown pass to Darius Cooper with just nine seconds left in the game.

Although not as impressive overall as other 2-0 sides, that ability to win games at the death is a familiar trait with Philly - and will make them dangerous all season again.

The New Orleans Saints just fell short after a monster comeback in Detroit last week, but went one better this week by upsetting Lamar Jackson's Baltimore Ravens 24-17 in their home opener.

Tyler Shough bundled over in a big crowd for a slightly controversial touchdown given the ball was largely unsighted, before two-time MVP Jackson then threw a late interception when trying to salvage the game.

The Saints may just surprise a few more teams this season.

Surprising everyone right now are the Las Vegas Raiders, who sit on 2-0 after winning 26-14 at the hapless Chargers.

The Chargers have lost by double digits to two of last season's biggest strugglers and with away games at Buffalo and Seattle, things look likely to get much worse.

DeShaun Watson threw a fourth quarter touchdown as the Cleveland Browns also sprung an upset win on the road in Tampa Bay, with a weather delay meaning they had to wait an extra two hours to seal the deal.

Perhaps the biggest surprise so far though is just how bad the Atlanta Falcons are. They were beaten 34-3 by the Carolina Panthers to become just the fourth team since 1978 to fail to get into an opponents red zone in their first two games.

The quarterback mess has played a part - and what summed them up nicely was undrafted rookie Jack Strand replacing a struggling Cooper Rush, and duly threw a pick six.

Atlanta could already be eyeing the first draft pick next year if this continues.

title: NFL intends to proceed with Ravens-Cowboys in Brazil, despite field concerns
description: When it comes to the NFL's obsession with expanding pro football's footprint, nothing will get in the way.
fullText:
When it comes to the NFL's obsession with expanding pro football's footprint, nothing will get in the way.

Concerns exist regarding the quality of the playing surface in Rio de Janeiro for next Sunday's game between the Ravens and Cowboys. The league, however, is undeterred.

Via Mark Maske of Front Office Sports, a league spokesperson said Sunday that (quoting Maske not the spokesperson) "the league is looking forward to the game in Rio and, as with all international games, it has a plan in place to ensure a high-quality playing surface."

Separately, the NFL Players Association told Maske that it's aware of the situation, and that it has been in touch with the league office about it.

Eight years ago, the NFL moved a Chiefs-Rams game from Mexico City to L.A. due to field concerns. However, the league has seemingly adopted a "damn the torpedoes" approach wen it comes to globalizing the game — and it doesn't seem to be inclined to let something like a less-than-ideal field get in the way.

title: Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase join exclusive NFL club in Bengals’ win vs. Texans
description: One of the greatest QB-WR duos in NFL history.
fullText:
Joe Burrow has started slowly in nearly every season of his career. He hasn't been prolific through two games this season, but he's been successful.

In addition, he's joined some elite company alongside his running mate, Ja'Marr Chase.

For only the second time in his career, Burrow has thrown for 200+ yards in each of his first two games of the season. Sunday in Houston, Burrow threw for 207 yards and two touchdowns on 20/31 passing with no interceptions.

Both touchdowns went to Chase, giving the duo 50 touchdown connections for their career. According to NFL researcher Arye Pulli, only four QB-WR duos in NFL history have hit that mark before reaching the age of 30, and the Burrow-Chase duo just joined the club.

Chase finished the game with seven catches for 75 yards and those two scores.

QB-WR duos in NFL history to reach 50 touchdown connections while both players were under 30:

🏈 Dan Marino — Mark Clayton
🏈 John Hadl — Lance Alworth
🏈 Daunte Culpepper — Randy Moss
🏈 Joe Burrow — Ja’Marr Chase

That’s the entire list.

Again, Burrow hasn't been prolific yet. But he's been productive and successful.

On Sunday, Burrow also showed his toughness as he dealt with back tightness during the week leading up to Sunday. Not ideal going up against the Texans' defense. But Burrow wasn't mincing words or backing down earlier this week when he said he was good to go.

On Sunday in Houston, Burrow went out and withstood five sacks, delivering a performance that helped the Bengals to a massive road win.

We've seen Burrow deliver performances like this while banged up and taking several hits in a game. Houston's defense is ferocious, and they sacked Burrow five times on Sunday. Yet Burrow extended plays, including the second touchdown to Chase and a 16-yard third-down pass to Samaje Perine.

Despite back tightness and Houston's defense, Burrow overcame it all, and the Bengals are now 2-0. Just wait till he starts posting prolific numbers.

title: Former Falcons QB tied for most TD passes in NFL after Week 2
description: Former Falcons QB Kirk Cousins has NFL-high six TD passes for 2-0 Raiders
fullText:
The Atlanta Falcons dropped to 0-2 after Sunday's embarrassing 34-3 blowout against the Carolina Panthers. Things got so bad that the Falcons turned to fourth-string quarterback Jack Strand in the third quarter of their Week 2 loss.

As if Sunday's game wasn't bad enough, former Falcons quarterback Kirk Cousins added insult to injury with his latest performance. Cousins passed for three touchdowns and an interception in the Raiders' 26-14 upset over the Los Angeles Chargers.

The 38-year-old is tied for the league lead with six touchdowns passes and has the Raiders sitting at 2-0 after Week 2. The Falcons released Cousins in March, ending his frustrating two-year run in Atlanta.

Las Vegas signed the veteran QB to help mentor No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, but they didn't make the mistake of giving Cousins $100 million in guaranteed money. Some thought the Falcons might bring back Cousins to reunite with Kevin Stefanski, but both sides needed a fresh start.

The Falcons have struggled to navigate their quarterback injuries thus far, and Cooper Rush hasn't gotten the job done. Rush was benched in the third quarter for Strand on Sunday, but the rookie didn't fare much better. Atlanta's quarterbacks combined to go 18/32 for 129 yards and three interceptions.

On the bright side, Michael Penix Jr. is expected to return next week. However, we will have to wait and see what Kevin Stefanski says on Monday morning.

title: Patriots vs. Steelers live updates: Score, news, discussion from NFL Week 2
description: The Patriots will host the Steelers in their 2026 home opener at Gillette Stadium.
fullText:
The New England Patriots began their 2026 regular season on the wrong foot. Dropping their opener against the world champion Seattle Seahawks, they have started their second campaign under head coach Mike Vrabel with an 0-1 record.

In order to improve to 1-1 and get their first victory of the season, the Patriots will have to defend their home turf against a Pittsburgh Steelers team that did win in Week 1. A win over Pittsburgh would not just mean a return to .500 on the year for New England, though, but also the first W in a home opener since the 2020 season.

Sunday, Sept. 20, 1 p.m. ET | Gillette Stadium (Foxborough, MA) | Broadcast information | Inactives | Game day roster | Weather forecast

The Patriots started the game on defense, and with a quick three-and-out. New England allowed just three combined yards on two Steelers carry, while Aaron Rodgers' decision to target Christian Gonzalez on the game's first third down led to an incompletion and subsequent punt.

New England's first offensive series started well, with Drake Maye completing passes to DeMario Douglas and Hunter Henry to move the unit into Steelers territory. However, the drive came to a quick and disappointing end when Rhamondre Stevenson lost a fumble on his second touch of the day.

Before even starting their next series, a taunting penalty against safety Jalen Ramsey backed the Steelers up at their own 16-yard line. Things did not get better for Rodgers and company from that point on: a short run was followed by Gabe Jacas forcing a throwaway and another incompletion on third down.

Marcus Jones gained 19 yards on his first punt return of the day, allowing the Patriots to begin their second drive on the Pittsburgh 49-yard line. It could have been a quick one, with a 10-yard Jalen Ramsey sack on third down seemingly ending the series. However, a defensive offsides penalty negated the play and gave New England another chance. TreVeyon Henderson took advantage of it: not only did he convert the subsequent 3rd-and-1, he followed it up with a 39-yard touchdown run on the very next play. | Patriots 7 : 0 Steelers

.@TreVeyonH4 took off.. WOW 🤯

📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/9kHGL49Bcv

After keeping the Steelers offense in check for the first two series, the unit did find some rhythm on its third. It did not matter: a well-time Robert Spillane blitz forced an incompletion on 3rd-and-6 in New England territory, while Pittsburgh kicker Chris Boswell sent the ensuing 57-yard field goal try wide to the left.

The Patriots offense continued to look good early into its next possession, quickly moving to the Pittsburgh side of the field again. Romeo Doubs caught his first pass as a Patriot, Rhamondre Stevenson converted a 3rd-and-1 after returning to the field following his fumble, and Drake Maye hit Eli Raridon for a 30-yard gain. However, once in the red zone, the unit ran into trouble: a Morgan Moses false start was followed by a 3-yard sack — a play that saw Mike Onwenu suffer an ankle injury. The right guard was carted off the field and quickly ruled out with an ankle injury.

Coming out of the quarter break, another sack led to the Patriots bringing out Andy Borregales. The second-year kickers split the uprights from 30 yards out to extend his team's lead. | Patriots 10 : 0 Steelers

The Patriots had a chance to quickly end the Steelers' first possession of the second quarter, but the offense was able to move the sticks on a 4th-and-1 to keep the series alive. The drive did take 6:50 off the clock and saw Pittsburgh march into potential scoring range, but it ended with a Christian Elliss/Robert Spillane double-team sack of Aaron Rodgers: the veteran quarterback lost the ball, with neither team able to scoop it up before Steelers left tackle Troy Fautanu did so back at the Pittsburgh 42 — a net loss of 36 yards to set up a 4th-and-43.

New England's offense struggled to find its footing on the next drive, even though a roughing the pass call and 10-yard completion to Mack Hollins allowed the team to move from deep into its own territory to a more comfortable position on the field. However, the series advanced no further than the 38-yard line and eventually ended in a 54-yard Mitch Wishnowsky punt.

New England's defense again did its job on the next drive. Although the Steelers gained two first downs — one via a 14-yard Travis Homer run, the other on a pass interference call against Kevin Byard — they eventually stalled after crossing midfield. An incomplete pass on 3rd-and-9 in the area of Marcus Jones prompted Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy to send out his punting unit for the fourth time in the first half.

The Patriots offense had a chance to double-dip before and after the half, but they struggled to get their offense going in the late second quarter. The series began with a 12-yard sack against Drake Maye, and the team opted to be conservative from that point on. Unfortunately for New England, that approach allowed the Steelers to get the ball back with 40 seconds left on the clock.

While Pittsburgh was unable to turn its next possession into a touchdown, it did manage to cut into the Patriots' 10-point lead when Chris Boswell scored a 56-yard field goal as time expired on the first half. | Patriots 10 : 3 Steelers

The Patriots flirted with a three-and-out to start their first drive of the second half, but Drake Maye moved out the pocket on 3rd-and-5 and found Romeo Dobbs for a 29-yard gain. However, one play later disaster struck: the second-year quarterback attempted a deep pass to Hunter Henry off his back foot and was easily intercepted by linebacker Patrick Queen.

New England's defense came close to forcing a quick three-and-out after the Maye interception, but Robert Spillane was flagged on third down to negate what would have been a stop. The punt did eventually come, however, after Rodgers threw incomplete on a 3rd-and-6.

After some offensive struggles in the late second and early third quarter, the Patriots found themselves with a scoring opportunity again in the late third period. The big play to get them there was a 29-yard Rhamondre Stevenson run that saw him evade a tackle attempt and gain extra yards after contact. However, the effort did not lead to any points: a blown up screen pass on third down set the stage for Andy Borregales missing a 47-yard field goal attempt wide right.

Just like they did after the interception, the Steelers were unable to capitalize on a Patriots miscue on their next drive. Two short gains were followed by a drop on 3rd-and-3 by DK Metcalf, who was once again being shadowed by Christian Gonzalez.

The Patriots started their next drive with a bang, a 63-yard pass completion from Maye to a wide-open Romeo Doubs. The offseason addition, who was held without a catch in last week's season opener, was able to work his way through Pittsburgh's zone coverage for New England's biggest play of the season. The team's offensive inconsistency reared its ugly head again right after that play — a delay of game penalty on first down followed by a quick throwaway on third down — but the ensuing Andy Borregales field goal try from 45 yards was good this time around. | Patriots 13 : 3 Steelers

Three plays into the fourth quarter, the Patriots defense finally registered its first takeaway of the season — and it was a big one. Christian Barmore knifed through the Steelers interior offensive line to get to Aaron Rodgers, strip-sacking the veteran quarterback. The loose football was picked up by teammate Elijah Ponder, who ran the fumble recovery back 19 yards for a touchdown. | Patriots 20 : 3 Steelers

STRIP SACK SCOOP & SCORE‼️

📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/8iXt4tlZS4

New England's defense kept the foot on the gas on the next Steelers drive. An incompletion was followed by a short pass to tight end Pat Freiermuth and finally Joshua Farmer recording his first career sack when he took down Aaron Rodgers for a loss of 11 to force another Pittsburgh punt.

Starting at its own 40-yard line and crossing into Pittsburgh territory two plays later, New England could have added to its lead on the next drive. However, the offense was unable to march any further and had to punt the ball back to the Steelers after Maye and Doubs failed to connect on a 3rd-and-9.

The Steelers came close to cutting into the Patriots' 17-point lead on the next drive, marching all the way to the New England 4-yard line. However, they ran into some stiff resistance at that point: first, Elijah Ponder sacked Aaron Rodgers for a loss of 13 yards; on the very next play, Charles Woods blew up a quick pass attempt that led to the ball popping up in the air and rookie Gabe Jacas intercepting it.

title: Chiefs star fined more than $8k ahead of 'SNF' matchup vs. Colts
description: The NFL fined Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III more than $8,000 ahead of Kansas City's Week 2 matchup against the Colts on 'Sunday Night Football.'
fullText:
Star running back Kenneth Walker III was fined $8,357 ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs' Week 2 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts on 'Sunday Night Football.'

The fine was levied after Walker unwisely decided to throw a football into the stands at Arrowhead Stadium after he scored a touchdown during the Chiefs' primetime win over the Denver Broncos in Week 1.

In one of the best performances of his career, Walker rushed for 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries against the Broncos. He also caught three passes for 18 yards and scored one receiving touchdown that helped lift Kansas City to victory.

Walker will have the opportunity to appeal the fine he incurred in Week 1, but given that his conduct was a clear violation of the NFL's player conduct policy, it is unlikely he would have a case to have the financial penalty reduced or cleared altogether.

The Texans traded up 13 places to get Watson, who had played college football at Clemson.

"Some on staff didn't want to extend Watson at all—most notably then–executive vice president of football operations Jack Easterby, who had arrived from New England in 2019 with designs on resetting the building and immediately had friction with Watson.

"While often electric on the field, he was frequently late to meetings, wanted increased influence over personnel and coaching decisions, and had trouble correcting some on-field shortcomings, such as a cadence that coaches felt was contributing to pre-snap penalties," wrote Pelissero on his Substack.

The Texans eventually ended up extending him on a four-year, $156 million deal. Watson only played one year before deciding to sit out the next, as he was looking for a trade away from the franchise.

Eventually, a few off-the-field issues came into the open, which ideally should have decreased his value, but the Cleveland Browns decided to give him a chance, and offered him a five-year $230 million deal.

Colin Kaepernick wants another chance in the NFL after nearly a decade away from the field. The former quarterback says he continues training hard and believes he can keep up with today's starters.

He has not played an official game since Jan. 1, 2017. Kaepernick has maintained that the league blacklisted him after his national anthem protest, but he continues preparing for the day a franchise finally calls.

Kaepernick's last NFL appearance came after the 2016 season, when his national anthem protest made him one of the league's most debated players. He has not joined a roster since, but he says preparation remains within his control.

"I have to do everything that is in my control to make sure that I'm prepared. And I mean that whether that's training, whether that's making sure I'm making the right calls. I want to make sure that what I have control over, I'm showing up the best way possible there," Kaepernick said.

He added, "I still train five days a week. I'm up at 4:30 in the morning doing my training before I go about the rest of my day."

Kaepernick follows quarterback stat lines to see which teams might need help. He has not received an offer, but he continues training for one. His routine is designed to keep him ready for an NFL workout.

Kaepernick previously reached Super Bowl XLVII with the San Francisco 49ers. A team would have to evaluate his current ability after years away from NFL competition. Kaepernick's argument is that his daily work should earn that opportunity.

Kaepernick's explanation for his absence is connected to an ownership dispute. According to a report, he alleged that Robert Kraft and other owners coordinated against Macklemore after the rapper criticized Israel.

Kaepernick said the situation reminded him of his grievance: "The part that I hope people appreciate and take away in this moment is what [New England Patriots owner] Robert Kraft and what they're saying by denying Macklemore the opportunity to go out and perform with Ed Sheeran is they are willing to collude."

He added, "The [NFL owners] are openly colluding."

Those remain Kaepernick's allegations, not a court finding against Kraft or the 32 owners. His 2017 grievance with Eric Reid was settled confidentially in 2019, so no public liability finding followed. The dispute remains part of his explanation for his absence.

Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken was the Tampa Bay Buccaneers offensive coordinator from 2016 through the 2018 season. The Bucs had a lot of success on offense under Monken, but things went sideways and the two parted ways.

Now that Monken is a head coach for the first time in his NFL career, he got a chance to reflect on the team that gave him his first real chance at calling plays in the NFL.

"I wouldn't be where I'm at without Dirk Koetter, who was the head coach there," admitted Monken. "He gave me the opportunity to call plays in '18, and that changed my track forever."

Monken gave a lot of credit to Koetter for being where he is now. However, he also noted that he still enjoys catching up with people in the front office that he sees around the NFL. From General Manager Jason Licht to other personnel and front office members, Monken listed off friends that he made in Tampa Bay.

"I consider people in the front office friends of mine," said Monken. "We just didn't win enough, but I really enjoyed it there; I grew as a coach."

The Bucs went 19-29 during the time that Monken was with the Buccaneers.

The Bucs went 9-7 in the first year that Monken was the offensive coordinator for Tampa Bay. However, as Monken noted, he was not calling plays. Was under an offensive-minded head coach who called the plays.

The team went 5-11 in the second year that Monken worked under Koetter. So, Koetter handed the playcalling to Monken. The offense thrived under Monken, but the defense let them down. They went 5-11 again and cleaned house.

Monken was hired from the college ranks. He was the Southern Miss head coach from 2016 through 2018 and was the Oklahoma State offensive coordinator before that. He was known for a high-flying offense, and the Bucs gave him a chance in the NFL in 2016.

After his stint with Tampa Bay, he was hired by Freddie Kitchens to be the offensive coordinator for Baker Mayfield with the Cleveland Browns. Now, Monken will face Mayfield against his old team.

Monken lasted just one year in Cleveland. Then, he went back to college as the Georgia offensive coordinator. He stayed from 2020 through 2022.

In 2023, he was hired as the Baltimore Ravens' offensive coordinator. He coached Lamar Jackson from 2023 through 2025, but when John Harbaugh resigned, the team moved on from Monken.

Now, he is back with the Cleveland Browns as their head coach. Monken is 60 years old, and got his first stint as a head coach in the NFL. His team lost 34-10 to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1.

Watson produced six catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1. So, Golden cannot quite dethrone him for the top spot.

title: Adrian Peterson Completes Court-Ordered Community Service in Minnesota DWI Case

fullText:
Adrian Peterson has completed the community-service requirement imposed after his 2025 Minnesota DWI arrest.

The former NFL MVP logged enough hours in July to satisfy the 32 hours ordered by the court, according to documents obtained by TMZ. The records show Peterson performed the work between July 13 and July 30.

His service included four-hour shifts with Meals on Wheels and a local food drive, along with work involving bags for homeless youth, a YMCA program and an event for senior citizens.

Completing those hours moves Peterson closer to resolving the Minnesota case, but community service was only one component of the sentence he received after pleading guilty earlier this year. His other conditions included a stayed jail sentence, a victim impact panel and restrictions tied to his probation.

Peterson pleaded guilty in March to one count of driving while impaired. Court documents showed that he received a 90-day sentence at the Hennepin County Adult Corrections Facility, but the jail term was stayed for one year as long as he complied with the court's conditions.

He was ordered to complete 32 hours of community service within 180 days and attend a victim impact panel. Peterson was also required to undergo an alcohol screening, which court records indicated he had already completed by the time the plea agreement was reported. The remaining charges were dismissed as part of the deal, according to TMZ.

The agreement also required Peterson to avoid alcohol- or drug-related offenses and reckless-driving offenses during the one-year period in which the jail sentence was stayed.

The case began in the early hours of April 25, 2025, after Peterson appeared at the Minnesota Vikings' NFL Draft event at U.S. Bank Stadium. A Minnesota State Patrol trooper stopped his Audi Q5 in Richfield at about 3:20 a.m. after seeing it travel 83 mph in a 55-mph zone.

A preliminary breath test measured Peterson's blood alcohol concentration at 0.14%, according to authorities. Minnesota's legal driving limit is 0.08%.

Peterson was booked into the Hennepin County Jail at 5:16 a.m. and released just over two hours later after posting $4,000 bond, the Associated Press reported.

Peterson's guilty plea addressed the charge stemming from the Minnesota stop, but he was arrested again on suspicion of DWI in Texas later in 2025.

Police in Sugar Land arrested Peterson in October after finding him asleep behind the wheel of a vehicle at a gas station, according to court records later reported by Reuters. Officers said the vehicle's engine was running and that Peterson showed signs of intoxication.

Police also reported finding a handgun inside the glove compartment, resulting in an additional charge of unlawfully carrying a weapon. Peterson was released from the Fort Bend County Jail on $3,000 bond.

Dating back to his days as an NFL quarterback, Ryan Fitzpatrick has been a favorite of both the media and fans.

The journeyman was a great quote for reporters and hosts, and lived up to the notion that backup quarterbacks are always the fan favorite on a team. Several of Fitzpatrick's late-season runs — in Houston, New York, Buffalo and Miami — will are still remembered fondly by the fans of those franchises.

Since joining the Prime Video crew on Thursday Night Football, Fitzpatrick has remained a daring darling of the football community. The big-bearded QB was in Buffalo for the opening of Highmark Stadium, and celebrated with a traditional leap through a folding table.

It went over great in the building, but somewhere in New York City, FS1's Nick Wright watched with bemusement. Friday on First Things First as the show aired a highlight of Fitzpatrick's table-crash, Wright questioned the hype.

"We don't need to promote this guy. It's enough. He gets plenty of promotion," Wright said.

"He made a nice career for himself. He's rebranded from, like, the Harvard smart quarterback, which never really made sense because if you watched him play, he looked like he might not be able to add. He was just crazy reckless. He was talented, but crazy reckless. And now, just because he has a long beard and we see his chest hair, he's charismatic? I don't get it."

Nick Wright isn’t feeling Ryan Fitzpatrick’s antics on TNF: “Just because he has a long beard and we see his chest hair, he’s charismatic? I don’t get it.” pic.twitter.com/NMHYAoEkpE

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) September 18, 2026

When Wright questioned why FTF would even play the clip, anchor Kevin Wildes said it was a cool moment for Fitzpatrick to set off the tradition at the new stadium.

"Everybody does that in Buffalo. Literally everybody does it," Wright responded. "We don't typically promote other networks' pregame shows, and if we're gonna do it, let's pick a good one."

In typical Wright fashion, he offered this barb with a chuckle and a smile. But you could hear the old radio host coming out of him; somewhere not too deep down, Wright clearly thinks Fitzpatrick is way too beloved.

These were not the only shots Wright fired on Friday's First Things First. Wright also joked about the supposed new rules of consumption on live television after ESPN viewers caught a glimpse of Pat McAfee seemingly smoking weed.

title: Saints' plan to keep Lamar Jackson in the pocket presents a major gamble
description: Saints' Carl Granderson wants Lamar Jackson kept in the pocket, but the Ravens quarterback remains among the NFL's most dangerous passers
fullText:
The New Orleans Saints know that letting Lamar Jackson escape the pocket can turn a productive defensive snap into an explosive play. Saints defensive end Carl Granderson believes discipline will be central to New Orleans' plan for containing the Baltimore Ravens quarterback Sunday at M&T Bank Stadium.

"We can't overthink it," Granderson said, via the NOF Network. "We just gotta go into the game, keep him in the pocket and play our game."

The approach is understandable, but keeping Jackson between the tackles does not eliminate the most dangerous parts of Baltimore's offense. The two-time NFL MVP has become one of the league's most efficient pocket passers and can punish defenses that get too focused on his running ability. Jackson completed 17 of 25 passes for 324 yards and one touchdown in Baltimore's 41-23 victory over Indianapolis. He averaged 13 yards per attempt, avoided an interception, and threw for more yards than in any game during the 2025 season.

#Saints DE Carl Granderson on containing #Ravens QB Lamar Jackson:

"We can't overthink it. We just gotta go into the game, keep him in the pocket and play our game." pic.twitter.com/0uLtFVBrdO

Jackson was also effective when offensive coordinator Declan Doyle placed him under center. He completed six of eight attempts for 114 yards from that alignment, including a 49-yard connection with Zay Flowers off a bootleg concept. His development as a passer predates Doyle's arrival. Jackson threw for 4,172 yards, 41 touchdowns and only four interceptions during his 2024 All-Pro season. He finished with a 119.6 passer rating, showing defenses cannot simply concede the pocket and expect Baltimore's passing game to become less efficient.

New Orleans must maintain rush-lane integrity because Jackson can still change the game as a runner. He converted a third-and-16 against Indianapolis by avoiding two defenders and scrambling for 16 yards. However, Granderson and the Saints cannot become passive while attempting to contain him. Jackson's patience, accuracy, and improved command from the pocket make him just as capable of dissecting a defense without crossing the line of scrimmage.

The Seahawks in their home opener scored 13 points while holding the Patriots to 10 points in the Super Bowl rematch. It seems as though, defensively, the Seahawks have not missed a beat. They struggled a bit offensively, but between Sam Darnold going down five snaps in, and having a first time play-caller calling their first regular season game, that is to be expected. In 2025, they scored an average of 29 points per game, while allowing and average 17 points per game. Averaging the points for comes out to 21 points, while averaging the points allowed comes to 14 points.

Per FTN's DVOA, the Seahawks are the ninth ranked team in total DVOA. They were the 20th ranked offense per DVOA, the fifth ranked defense, and the fourth ranked special teams. It's worth noting that DVOA takes several weeks into the season before it becomes a more stable metric. There's also no accounting for Seattle having Drew Lock come into the game due to Sam Darnold's injury.

Per Sumer Sports, the Seahawks were the 14th ranked offense in total EPA and EPA per play. On defense, they were the 11th ranked defense in total EPA and the 12th ranked defense in EPA per play.

The Cardinals put up 26 in their upset road win over the Los Angeles Chargers. They held Justin Herbert and the Chargers offense to just 14 points. Arizona looked good in its first game of the season, and it seems first-year head coach Mike LaFleur has the team buttoned up. Last season, the Cardinals averaged 22 points a game while allowing opponents to score 29 points. Their overall average points for is 24, while their averaged points allowed is 22.

Per DVOA, the Cardinals were ranked the 13th best team in the NFL after Week One. They had the sixth ranked offense per DVOA, 20th ranked defense, and 18th ranked special teams.

Per Sumer Sports, the Cardinals have the 10th ranked team per total EPA on offense as well as EPA per play on offense. They were also the fifth ranked team per total EPA on defense and fifth in EPA per play on defense.

Seahawks 21 + Cards opponents 22 = 43 / 2 = 21.5 Points for Seahawks, but since you cannot have half a point, lets round up to 22.

Cards 24 + Sea opponents 14 = 38 / 2 = 19 Points for Seahawks

Seahawks score 7 more points on average than opponents. 19 – 4 = 15.

Initial score prediction: 22 – 15, Seahawks win

However, to make this score work, the Seahawks would need to go for a 2-point conversion, and that doesn't make a ton of sense, so let's make some adjustments.

Three touchdowns for the Seahawks make sense. I think Jaxon Smith-Njigba and AJ Barner are likely to get one apiece, and I think Jadarian Price will get his first touchdown in this game. Add those points together with some Jason Myers extra points, and we get 21.

Final Score Prediction: 21 – 15, Seahawks Victory

title: NFL Week 2 picks & predictions: Patriots face 0-2 crisis
description: Several preseason Super Bowl contenders are looking to avoid 0-2 starts in NFL Week 2.
fullText:
NFL Week 2 can be pivotal for several teams looking to avoid an 0-2 start, including the Houston Texans and New England Patriots.

The first weekend of action delivered memorable games, including the Chicago Bears and Jacksonville Jaguars looking excellent on offense. Meanwhile, several disappointing results came by way of the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers and Patriots.

Last week, we put together a strong start to the 2026 season with a 10-5 pick record. We'll look to improve on that as the NFL slate shifts to Week 2.

Let's jump into this week's action with 16 games to choose from on the NFL docket.

Detroit Lions vs.Buffalo Bills (8:15 p.m. ET, Prime Video)

Both teams enter Week 2 with 1-0 records, but the Lions certainly benefitted from good fortune against the New Orleans Saints. Detroit certainly struggled to put away the Saints, and Josh Allen and Co. will be tougher.

The Bills enter the second week of the season with a lot of confidence after taking down the Houston Texans. Buffalo's strong offensive output is encouraging after D.J. Moore got into the end zone in his team debut. Pick: Bills 27, Lions 21

Carolina Panthers vs. Atlanta Falcons (1 p.m. ET, FOX)

The entire NFC South enters Week 2 winless, but the good news for Carolina and Atlanta is one team has a good shot at picking up their first win.

The Panthers offense showed they can be dynamic against the Chicago Bears. Bryce Young and Co. will likely carry that form over against the Falcons. Pick: Panthers 30, Falcons 20

New Orleans Saints vs. Baltimore Ravens (1 p.m. ET, CBS)

Baltimore's depleted receiving group is a massive concern against a pesky Saints team. However, do the Ravens need more than Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry to succeed?

New Orleans drops to 0-2 on the season while the Ravens continue to make an argument as the best team in the AFC. Pick: Ravens 21, Saints 17

Minnesota Vikings vs. Chicago Bears (1 p.m. ET, FOX)

The Bears are on a mission to score the most points in NFL history, but the Vikings defense will be a much tougher test than Carolina. Meanwhile, Minnesota will likely need to rely on Carson Wentz for another game as Kyler Murray heals from a concussion.

Chicago has an assortment of offensive weapons, including Rome Odunze and Coltson Loveland. That could prove to be too much for the Vikings to handle. Pick: Bears 27, Vikings 24

Cincinnati Bengals vs. Houston Texans (1 p.m. ET, CBS)

The Bengals are looking to go 2-0 after taking down the Buccaneers in Week 1. However, Joe Burrow's status for the game is certainly something to watch.

Maye and New England are facing a major crisis without A.J. Brown for at least the next six weeks. The Patriots' chances of returning to the Super Bowl could be in trouble without another loss in Week 2.

Pittsburgh didn't look impressive at times against Atlanta, but Aaron Rodgers has the benefit of a strong defense. T.J. Watt and the defense can hone in on the Patriots run game with very few pass-catching threats. Pick: Steelers 23, Patriots 17

Green Bay Packers vs. New York Jets (1 p.m. ET, FOX)

Green Bay is in a tough spot after facing ridicule across the league from their Week 1 collapse. Matt LeFleur needs a win and the Jets are typically a get-right game for many teams.

The Packers avoid an 0-2 start and silence the critics for at least one week. Pick: Packers 28, Jets 24

Cleveland Browns vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1 p.m. ET, CBS)

Tampa Bay's strong offense led by Baker Mayfield puts up a win after a tough loss against Joe Burrow and the Bengals. Cleveland might have to strongly consider benching DeShaun Watson if he struggles again in Week 2. Pick: Buccaneers 30, Browns 14

Philadelphia Eagles vs. Tennessee Titans (1 p.m. ET, FOX)

Tennessee looked completely out of sorts against the Jets, and the Eagles boast way more firepower. Jalen Hurts and Co. can look to establish the run a bit more with Saquon Barkley after a slow start.

Meanwhile, the Titans are destined to fall to 0-2 and stir up some early-season troubles for Brian Daboll. Pick: Eagles 34, Titans 21

Jim Harbaugh and Los Angeles produce in a big way and get to 1-1 before facing Buffalo next week. Pick: Chargers 37, Raiders 17

Another week without Sam Darnold means the Seahawks need to rely heavily on their defense. Drew Lock is competent, but it's a tough ask to play mistake-free for two consecutive weeks.

title: Start 'Em, Sit 'Em D/STs for Week 2 fantasy football
description: Your D/ST selection in fantasy football can be the difference between winning and losing. Here are our start/sit recommendations for NFL Week 2.
fullText:
It's a word that has seen public opinion shift in recent years, going from a cheap new concept to something that is extracting every last dollar out of your wallet – especially if sports are your thing. Streaming was supposed to take away the need for cable, letting people buy what they want without breaking the bank.

And where did that get us? Right back to cable, but in streaming form.

Just like your viewing habits, picking the right fantasy football D/ST week to week is a lot like finding the right streamer. After all, few will find a unit that is startable every week of the season. If you do, be sure to hold on to it.

For the rest of us, we are left to play the matchups and hope for the best. At least in this case, the price isn't going up every couple of months.

Here are the fantasy defenses to start and others that should sit in Week 2.

Cam Ward didn't turn the ball over in Week 1, which could be problematic from a fantasy football standpoint. However, he could feel the need to force it in Week 2 as the Titans try to put together something that resembles an NFL offense.

One way or another, the Jets defense was living in the Tennessee backfield throughout Week 1 and Ward was running for his life. The second-year quarterback was slippery in the pocket, but the Eagles will present an even bigger challenge. This could be a big number from Vic Fangio's unit.

The Chiefs smothered the Broncos offense last week. Denver couldn't run the ball, couldn't throw the ball and, essentially, couldn't have the ball. It was an old-fashioned beatdown in Kansas City, reminding NFL fans of who the Chiefs are.

You could point to the new play-caller in Davis Webb for Denver, but this is still a much more talented unit than the one going into Arrowhead in Week 2. Daniel Jones seems to have lost some of the magic and Jonathan Taylor can't do it all alone. Steve Spagnuolo should be salivating at this matchup.

Flip the script. That is the goal for the Patriots in Week 2 after laying an egg against the Seahawks on opening night. New England had no business losing that game after Drew Lock entered for the injured Sam Darnold, but Mike Vrabel's team found a way anyway. It wasn't the defense's fault, however.

Despite some horrendous offense, the Patriots still held the Seahawks to just 13 points and we should expect more of the same against the Steelers. Aaron Rodgers isn't a threat to run and DK Metcalf will have to deal with Christian Gonzalez – and we know how that typically goes. With Rodgers averaging just 5.5 yards per attempt in Week 1, New England can crowd the line of scrimmage without much fear of being beat over the top.

The Bucs just gave up 33 points to the Bengals in Week 1, mostly because their offense produced more turnovers than your favorite bakery. It just so happens that Baker Mayfield was a key reason for that, losing three fumbles in the contest all by himself. One of Tampa's four turnovers did result in a touchdown, so we can't blame the defense for that.

Luckily for the Bucs, Week 2 is much easier against a lifeless Browns team. If a Deshaun Watson-led offense puts together a solid showing and ruins the day for this fantasy defense, we'll just have to tip our cap. Don't bet on that happening though.

It was a week to forget for one of the NFL's best defenses. Houston gave up 36 points and recorded just two sacks against Buffalo in Week 1, and they failed to force a turnover. You can easily dismiss the performance since the Bills were on the opposite sideline, but the Texans' Week 2 opponent is no cupcake.

The Bengals scored 33 points in the opener and that was without Ja'Marr Chase making an impact. While there's a good chance that the Texans were the first defense off the board in your draft, we can't in good faith recommend starting them. If there's a better matchup available, don't hesitate to take it.

Life without Micah Parsons hasn't been kind to the Packers. They are now on a five-game losing streak without the star defender, which is actually six if you include the game when he got hurt. Green Bay is in danger of stretching that streak to seven in the Meadowlands, where it will take on a frisky Jets team that is riding high after Week 1.

With some rain in the forecast, that bodes well for the Jets. They can lean on a solid offensive line and another run-heavy game script against a Packers team that just gave up a pair of rushing scores in the opener. And who could possibly forget the 22 unanswered points that the Vikings scored in the fourth quarter? Don't be surprised if that hangs over Matt LaFleur's group in Week 2.

Speaking of teams that deserve a little more credit, how about the Cardinals? No one gave them a chance to win in Week 1. Not only did they win, but they also did it in dominant fashion against the Super Bowl-contending Chargers. Now for an encore, Arizona only has to match up against the defending Super Bowl champions.

However, let's not forget that Lock is the starter and that increases the potential for turnovers from the Seahawks offense. Turnovers lead to short fields, short fields lead to points, points lead to fantasy defense sadness. Yet that isn't the Cardinals' only chance in Week 2, considering Mike LaFleur has put together a competent offense. This could be a letdown spot for the Seahawks after celebrating the Super Bowl win and losing Darnold all in one night. This will be their first test without him for an entire game, against a divisional opponent. Seattle's defense can ride the bench this week.

Myles Garrett was invisible in Week 1. He will miss Week 2 after knee surgery. Garrett might not be the only star in this loaded L.A. defense, but he is certainly the biggest one. The Giants won't have to deal with the pass-rusher, which only helps their chances.

John Harbaugh's team proved to be a physical, pesky group in Week 1. Between Jaxson Dart's legs and Cam Skattebo's tough running style, these aren't the Giants of old. After playing in Australia last week, the Giants are one of those teams that Sean McVay's sleepy bunch won't want to see. This game could be closer than expected and that won't bode well for the Rams' D/ST unit.

title: NFL Hands Down Decision on Texans’ Azeez Al-Shaair, 3 Key Stars After Bills Game Incident
description: Houston Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was fined $11,492 by the NFL for writing “Hind Rajab” on his eye black during the Week 1 loss to the Buffalo Bills. It is his second fine for an unauthorized message, after the league fined him $11,593 last January for writing “Stop The Genocide” during the playoff win over […] The post NFL Hands Down Decision on Texans’ Azeez Al-Shaair, 3 Key Stars After Bills Game Incident appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Houston Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was fined $11,492 by the NFL for writing "Hind Rajab" on his eye black during the Week 1 loss to the Buffalo Bills. It is his second fine for an unauthorized message, after the league fined him $11,593 last January for writing "Stop The Genocide" during the playoff win over Pittsburgh.

Hind Rajab was a five-year-old Palestinian girl killed in Gaza City in January 2024, and Al-Shaair has made clear he intends to keep using his platform regardless of the cost.

Three of his teammates were also fined as part of the same round of penalties. Al-Shaair, who is Muslim, has used his platform consistently to draw attention to the conflict, wearing "Free Palestine" cleats through the NFL's My Cause My Cleats program and hosting child amputees from Gaza at Texans games.

Al-Shaair addressed the fine directly, making clear he understood the consequences before he took the field.

"At the end of the day, it's bigger than me," Al-Shaair told Aaron Wilson. "The things that are going on make people uncomfortable, imagine how those people feel. I think that's the biggest thing. I have no affiliation, no connection to these people other than the fact that I'm a human being."

He also added, "If you have a heart and you're a human being you can see what's going on in the world and you check yourself real quick. Even when I'm walking off this field, that's the type of stuff that goes through my head that I have to check myself when I'm sitting here crying about football when there's people dying every single day. If my platform can bring even a little hope to families in Palestine, then that is what I want to use it for."

After his January fine, Al-Shaair also pushed back on the threat of being removed from the game entirely. "I never seen Stef get pulled out of a game for having eye tape with writing on it," he said, referencing Stefon Diggs.

The fine was issued under Rule 6, Section 4, Article 8 of the NFL rulebook, which bans personal messages on game day equipment unless approved in advance by the league. The NFL does not grant approval for messages related to political causes. CAIR-Houston pointed out that the league fined Al-Shaair while allowing players to wear pins supporting the Stand Up to Jewish Hate campaign led by Patriots owner Robert Kraft.

Al-Shaair's bigger issue was that officials threatened to pull him from the game during the playoff win over Pittsburgh if he kept the message on. When addressing the matter, Al-Shaair brought up Stefon Diggs by name, pointing to the fact that his former teammate had written messages on his eye tape for years without ever being pulled from a game for it.

"I was told that if I wore that in the game, I would be pulled out the game," Al-Shaair said. "That was the part that I was confused about, because I understood it was a fine, but I ain't never seen Stef get pulled out the game for having eye tape with writing on it."

Diggs, who played alongside Al-Shaair in Houston last season before signing with New England, has written personal messages on his eye tape multiple times without ever being pulled from a game. That included a tribute to his brother Trevon after Trevon suffered a torn ACL in 2023, and a "Free Chap" message during a game in October 2024 while still with the Texans. He was fined for those but never removed from the field, which is exactly the inconsistency Al-Shaair was pointing to.

title: Bijan Robinson did something Week 1 no NFL player has in 40 years
description: Falcons RB almost beats 1986 record by Eric Dickerson
fullText:
Perhaps the most frustrating thing about the Atlanta Falcons' ongoing dumpster fire at quarterback is that it's wasting the prime years of some very special skill players - especially fourth-year stud Bijan Robinson.

Atlanta's superstar running back just passed Devonta Freeman on the franchise's all-time rushing list, and at the same time Robinson was so dominant in Week 1 that he came close to beating a fiendish 40-year NFL record set by Rams legend Eric Dickerson. Kevin Patra at NFL.com has the details.

"Bijan Robinson generated 173 scrimmage yards, including 90 receiving yards, most among all RBs through Sunday. Robinson accounted for 65.8% of the Falcons' yards from scrimmage in Week 1, the highest share by any player in a team's season opener since Rams RB Eric Dickerson (66.6%) in 1986."

Dickerson went on to make six Pro Bowl teams, earn five first-team All-Pro honors and eventually made the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Along the way, Dickerson won multiple Offensive Player of the Year awards and made the Hall of Fame all 80's team. He appeared in seven career playoff games, averaging over 100 yards in those contests and scoring three touchdowns.

The only thing missing from Dickerson's resume was a Super Bowl win - and right now it looks like Bijan Robinson's career path is on a similar trajectory. Somebody needs to find the final piece of the puzzle and give Robinson, Drake London and the rest of the gang a legitimate chance to win a ring.

title: 49ers RB Kaelon Black earns rare rookie trust after NFL debut

fullText:

title: Joey Porter Jr. Trade Rumors: Top NFL Insider Says Steelers Fans Should Monitor These Teams

Amid an unresolved contract situation, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport identified the Chiefs and Lions as two teams to watch if Pittsburgh ultimately decides to trade Joey Porter Jr.

Rapoport's comments on Tuesday's edition of "The Pat McAfee Show" come as the Steelers remain at an impasse with their cornerback over a contract extension. They have reportedly indicated they are willing to listen to trade offers.

"The Steelers have said that Joey Porter Jr is ramping up and then there's the contract part of it..

There are some teams that need corners and he's a very good player..

Pittsburgh has been open to trading him..

I would keep an eye on the Chiefs and Lions"@RapSheet#PMSLivepic.twitter.com/mJEgXxhzlO

Porter missed Pittsburgh's Week 1 win over Atlanta after dealing with a back injury. Head coach Mike McCarthy said the decision to keep Porter inactive was his, citing Porter's limited preparation.

While Rapoport didn't say a trade is imminent, Detroit's interest in Porter appears to be legitimate. The Lions have reportedly approached Pittsburgh about a potential trade.

Detroit's secondary was exposed in the second half of its Week 1 win over the Saints, allowing six completions of at least 20 yards. Saints wide receiver Chris Olave finished with 10 catches for 182 yards, highlighting the need for a cornerback capable of holding up against opposing No. 1 receivers.

Sports Illustrated's John Maakaron identified Detroit as the team best suited to make a "splash trade" for the Steelers cornerback, pointing to Porter's ability to play press-man coverage and hold his own without safety help. That would give defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard more flexibility to use aggressive pressure packages.

The Chiefs have a clear need at cornerback after trading Trent McDuffie to the Rams during the offseason. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane, who was selected with the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, suffered a shoulder injury after intercepting Bo Nix on Monday night.

"If Delane is hurt, [Chiefs general manager] Brett Veach will make a trade," Rapoport said. "He'll be risky. He'll make a trade."

Porter's contract demands could make a potential trade complicated because of the Chiefs' tight cap situation. He's entering the final year of his rookie deal, meaning any team trading for him would need to consider the cost of a long-term extension in addition to the draft capital or players being sent out.

Only former Chiefs star Tony Gonzalez (15,127) has more receiving yards in the position than Kelce (13,073).

title: Bears, Bills and Ravens win on record-breaking Sunday
description: After kicking off the NFL season with a Super Bowl rematch and a trip to Australia, week one continued with a record-breaking Sunday.
fullText:
After kicking off the season with a Super Bowl rematch and a trip to Australia, week one continued with a record-breaking Sunday.

The Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens showed why they are favourites to win the AFC Conference, and the Chicago Bears made a statement as they racked up 59 points.

Those wins contributed to an NFL record for the most points scored on the opening Sunday of the season since the league merger in 1970.

Here's what you need to know from the opening weekend.

The Bills changed their head coach in a bid to finally reach the Super Bowl with star quarterback Josh Allen, promoting offensive co-ordinator Joe Brady to the top job.

His first game was a big test, coming against last season's meanest defence, and the lead changed hands eight times in a thriller at the Houston Texans.

Running back David Montgomery scored three touchdowns on his Houston debut, but Allen ran in two touchdowns and passed for two more.

The 2024 season's Most Valuable Player was almost intercepted as he launched a hopeful pass into the endzone with less than two minutes remaining.

But on the next play 30-year-old Allen held his nerve with a 34-yard throw to Joshua Palmer that clinched a 36-31 win.

Buffalo's first five games are against potential Super Bowl contenders, so they needed to hit the ground running.

After missing last season's play-offs the Baltimore Ravens brought an end to John Harbaugh's 18-year tenure as head coach, and they made a flying start under successor Jesse Minter.

Zay Flowers, who became the NFL's fourth highest-paid wide receiver in the off-season, made five catches for a career-high 150 yards and a touchdown in the first half alone at the Indianapolis Colts.

Derrick Henry also scored twice before half-time to move into third on the all-time list for rushing touchdowns, then added another as the Ravens cruised to a 41-23 win.

But there was concern for Baltimore as Flowers and rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane missed the second half with hamstring and wrist injuries respectively.

The Ravens' impressive win was soon eclipsed by the Chicago Bears, who were level with the Carolina Panthers at 31-31 midway through the third quarter before romping to victory.

Running back D'Andre Swift finished with three touchdowns in a 59-37 road win - the highest-scoring week one game in NFL history and Chicago's highest score since 1980.

After leading the Bears to their first division title in seven years last season, head coach Ben Johnson has set some lofty targets.

"We want to be the highest scoring. We want to have the most wins. We want to win Super Bowls," he said.

Harbaugh is now in charge of a promising young roster at the New York Giants, and his first game came on a poignant night at the MetLife Stadium, which hosted the football World Cup final in July.

Two days after the 25th anniversary of 9/11, the Giants honoured New York's first responders and those impacted by the attacks with a series of tributes before Sunday's primetime game.

The Giants then produced a convincing 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys, with second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart passing for 230 yards and three touchdowns, while fit-again running back Cam Skattebo rushed for another.

It was a balanced team performance with a disciplined defence, a trademark of Harbaugh's team throughout his time in Baltimore.

With the New York Knicks ending their long wait for an NBA championship this year, there is genuine belief that the Giants can also get back in play-off contention.

The Arizona Cardinals have been tipped by many to finish with the NFL's worst record, while the Los Angeles Chargers are seen as play-off contenders.

But the Chargers were humbled on their own turf at SoFi Stadium, which will host Super Bowl 61 in February.

The Cardinals are trying to make a fresh start having brought in Mike LaFleur as head coach and released quarterback Kyler Murray, and they dominated possession in a 26-14 win.

Murray, who went on to earn the starting role with the Minnesota Vikings, made a wretched start at home to the Green Bay Packers, coached by LaFleur's older brother Matt.

Murray's first pass with the Vikings was intercepted, and the former first overall draft pick then suffered a concussion before being replaced by veteran Carson Wentz.

Despite falling 22-10 down late in the third quarter, the Vikings fought back to win 39-22, with Justin Jefferson claiming two well-taken touchdowns and a two-point conversion.

The Vikings have had nine starting quarterbacks since Jefferson was named offensive player of the year for 2022, and the wide receiver looked back to his best.

Although the Cincinnati Bengals have one of the NFL's most potent offences, they have been let down by their defence in the past three seasons.

The front office tried to remedy that in the off-season, and the revamped defence was impressive in their opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Three of last season's 11 defeats came despite scoring at least 34 points, and again the Bengals had little trouble scoring against the Bucs.

This time their defence did their job too, though, recording four sacks and forcing four fumbles. All four were recovered by Cincinnati, with one returned for a defensive touchdown in a 33-27 home win.

If the Bengals can maintain that consistency - and quarterback Joe Burrow avoids another injury-hit season - they could have realistic hope of returning to the Super Bowl, having played the last time the big game was held in LA in 2022.

title: NFL "trying all sorts of legal maneuvers" to get Josh Jacobs video
description: Jacobs will remain on paid leave while NFL reviews the case.
fullText:
The regular season opens with Packers running back Josh Jacobs on paid leave. He'll remain there while the NFL determines his punishment under the Personal Conduct Policy after a recent no-contest plea to multiple misdemeanor charges, including battery.

As Ian Rapoport of NFL Network explained on Sunday morning, the NFL will be meeting with Jacobs; that's always part of any review under the Personal Conduct Policy. Per Rapoport, the league also wants to see the video of the altercation, which was captured by a surveillance system in Jacobs's home — and which was placed under seal by the judge presiding over his criminal case.

Rapoport said the league is "trying all sorts of legal maneuvers" to get the video. No specific maneuver was mentioned.

The judge sealed the evidence in the case, including the video, at Jacobs's request. The NFL could, if it wanted, tell Jacobs he won't play until he asks for and receives a reversal of the order his lawyers sought.

Jacobs will receive credit for any games missed while on paid leave. But he won't be playing until the internal review is completed, along with any appeal.

That puts pressure on Jacobs to give the NFL whatever it needs before it can make a decision. It also sets the stage for a negotiated suspension, which would become final once an agreement is reached.

Six games is the baseline suspension for "domestic violence, dating violence, child abuse and other forms of family violence." Aggravating factors can increase the punishment.

Given the league's experiences with the Ray Rice case, it's hard to envision the matter being finalized without the NFL first seeing the video. If a suspension is imposed and the video is later released, it could (depending on the video's contents) creatie a major problem for the league, like the Rice video did in 2014.

title: Rapoport: NFL attempting to get their hands on the Josh Jacobs video
description: Apparently, the NFL hasn’t seen the Josh Jacobs video, either
fullText:
NFL Network/ESPN's Ian Rapoport reported on Sunday morning that the NFL is attempting to obtain the alleged video from the incident that led to Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs being charged with battery and criminal damage to property. Here is what Rapoport said, specifically:

The NFL wants to interview Josh Jacobs. That will happen. They're also trying all sorts of legal maneuvers to try to get the video of the incident that has since been barred by the court. So we'll see if the NFL is able to do that before suspending him.

From @NFLGameDay Morning (in-studio!): The #Falcons won’t have QB Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) today, but Michael Penix Jr could next week or Week 3; Meanwhile, the NFL is attempting to obtain the Josh Jacobs video for its investigation. pic.twitter.com/fqGbuA1Rv8

This video was first mentioned when Jacobs was officially charged by the Brown County District Attorney. According to the police report, the video was obtained via surveillance footage from inside the garage at Jacobs' residence. The county claimed that the video "corroborates the relevant portions of [anonymous victim]'s statement." According to the police report, it shows both Jacobs and the alleged victim leaving and returning to the residence and "the altercation."

Per the county, the victim attempted to leave the residence through the garage, as she believed her calls to the police were not going through due to poor service, and was followed by Jacobs. At that point, Jacobs "grabbed her and threw her to the ground and she struck her head, suffering an injury."

The video apparently confirms that after the victim was on the floor for around 40 seconds, Jacobs returned to the garage to damage the victim's phone — the second phone in the incident, after Jacobs apparently took the first phone from the anonymous woman and left his residence with the phone in his vehicle.

Jacobs pled no contest to the charges of battery and criminal damage to property on Thursday.

In court, District Attorney David Lasse stated that "videos weren't readily accessible on the device and had to be recovered." No further details were given about why a digital forensics unit had to recover the video from the surveillance system.

When the judge stated that he was going to treat pleas of no contest as pleas of guilty, Jacobs confirmed he understood and did not change his plea. When Jacobs was asked by the judge if he believed that the state could prove the elements of battery and the elements of criminal damage to property beyond a reasonable doubt had the case gone to a jury trial and would be "guilty as charged of those offenses," Jacobs also stated, "Yes."

The charge of criminal damage to property was deferred, meaning that it will come off Jacobs' record if he can stay out of the court system for 12 months, avoid contact with the victim, comply with supervision from the Brown County Criminal Justice Services, attend counseling that includes a batterer's prevention program and pay restitution to the victim. If Jacobs can accomplish that, the criminal damage to property charge will be dismissed, but the battery charge will remain on his record regardless. Should Jacobs break any condition of his deferred charge, he could serve up to nine months in jail — as the judge stated that he will sentence Jacobs to the maximum time allowed if it's found that Jacobs has a "material breach" of their agreement after a trial.

Later on that day, Judge Marc Hammer temporarily sealed the evidence in the case, including video recordings, at the request of Jacobs' attorneys.
