title: Fantasy football Start ‘Em, Sit ‘Em: 23 players to start or sit in Week 1
description: The first week of the 2026 NFL season is underway and we've already seen two games played. Here's our start/sit advice for your lineup on Sunday.
fullText:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season is officially underway, and fantasy football managers already have plenty to think about.

The defending champion Seattle Seahawks opened the season with a Super Bowl rematch against the Patriots, picking up a win. The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams squared off in Melbourne, Australia one night later, giving fans an early taste of what promises to be another unpredictable NFL season.

Now, the wait is over for the rest of the league. A full schedule of games is on tap Sunday, followed by the first "Monday Night Football" matchup of the season. With several divisional battles on the schedule, there are plenty of intriguing games – and fantasy storylines.

Of course, Week 1 is always one of the most difficult weeks to navigate in fantasy football. Managers who drafted A.J. Brown or Brock Bowers are already dealing with uncertainty moving forward, while those who landed Jaxon Smith-Njigba or Mike Evans can feel a little more comfortable about their lineups.

With 28 of 32 teams set to take the field Sunday and Monday, fantasy managers have some difficult decisions to make before kickoff. If you're on the fence about who to start, who to sit or which players could make the biggest impact in Week 1, we've got you covered.

Here are our start 'em and sit 'em recommendations for Week 1 of the 2026 fantasy football season:

The Saints are actually better against quarterbacks than most realize, as they allowed the eighth-fewest fantasy points per game (FPPG) to quarterbacks last season. Even so, Goff is close to a must-start given his proven track record of success in Detroit.

Goff has been one of the most consistent quarterbacks in fantasy football the last three seasons, never throwing for fewer than 4,500 yards or 30 touchdowns. That consistency – along with a strong Lions supporting cast that features Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Sam LaPorta and Jahmyr Gibbs – makes Goff a high-floor start.

Herbert was able to log a strong fantasy season in 2025 despite being pressured a league-high 288 times, per Pro Football Focus. He should have an easier time staying clean in 2026, with tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt in the fold, and that could raise his ceiling.

Even if Herbert's protection doesn't take an immediate step forward, he shouldn't have any issues against the Cardinals. Arizona had a 31.6% pressure rate last year, which ranked 26th in the league, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. The Cardinals didn't upgrade their edge rush rotation during the offseason, so Herbert should have plenty of time to pick apart a shaky-looking Arizona defense that surrendered 30.75 points per game during the preseason.

Prescott attempted the second-most passes in the NFL last season behind only Bo Nix. The 33-year-old may not be asked to throw quite as much in 2026, as Dallas' defense looks significantly improved from its league-worst unit last year, but he should still do more than enough to be a top-10 fantasy quarterback.

The Giants struggled to contain opposing quarterbacks last season, surrendering the eighth-most FPPG to the position. Prescott threw for 361 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in his lone full outing against New York, so he could be similarly positioned to thrive to open the fantasy season.

The Cowboys spent a lot of resources during the offseason to upgrade their defense, adding players like Rashan Gary, Jalen Thompson and first-round pick Caleb Downs to the fold. Christian Parker, who comes from the Vic Fangio coaching tree, could eventually lead the unit to success, but it may take time to gel early in the season.

If that happens, Dart should be positioned to take advantage of a Cowboys defense that allowed the most FPPG to quarterbacks last season. That included a league-high eight rushing touchdowns to the position, a stat that marries well with Dart's dual-threat capabilities.

The Browns suffered a couple of major losses on defense over the offseason. The aforementioned Garrett was traded to the Rams while defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz left the team after being passed over for Cleveland's head coaching job in favor of Todd Monken.

Despite these departures, the Browns are still returning most of their 2025 starters, and their defense ranked fourth in defensive EPA allowed per play last season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. That may make it hard for Lawrence – who was buoyed by an outlier nine rushing touchdowns in 2025 – to find high-level success in his first game of the 2026 campaign.

Mahomes is expected to play in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season despite tearing his left ACL and LCL during a December 2025 game against the Los Angeles Chargers. The 30-year-old quarterback may need time to shake off the rust, so it's fair to assume he might get off to a slower start than usual in 2026.

Further complicating Mahomes' path toward a productive fantasy day is that the Broncos have one of the NFL's best defenses. They have enjoyed particular success against Mahomes, who hasn't scored multiple touchdowns in a game against the Broncos since 2022, so it's best to steer clear of the two-time MVP.

Bucky is a sleeper entering 2026 after an injury-riddled season. Before his injury, through the first four weeks of 2025, Irving was third among all RBs in receptions (19) and receiving yards per game (48.3). Irving should excel in this one as a receiver and on the ground against the Bengals defense, which allowed the most fantasy points per game to running backs last season.

Cincinnati ranked 32nd in rushing yards allowed (147.1 per game) and 31st in yards per carry allowed (5.21). They added Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen on the defensive line, but don't let that stop you from trusting Bucky in Week 1. This game has the highest projected total of the week (50.5), so there should be plenty of fantasy goodness to be had.

The Texans' new weapon has a strong Week 1 matchup in his debut. The Bills surrendered the eighth-most fantasy points per game to backs a season ago, including the most rushing touchdowns to opposing backfields.

The Texans ranked eighth in RB rush attempts in 2025, so Montgomery should see plenty of opportunities with his new team. He has also ranked top 10 in goal-to-go rush attempts in six of his seven career seasons, so he's likely to find paydirt in this one. He's a rock-solid RB2 for fantasy managers with legitimate touchdown upside.

Williams staked his claim as one of the top breakout stars in 2025 and cashed in during the offseason with a contract extension in Dallas. He should eat in Week 1 against the Giants on "Sunday Night Football" at MetLife. New York traded away Dexter Lawrence and has done little to fill the void he left behind in run defense that ranked 31st against the run in 2025, allowing 145.3 rushing yards per game and the fifth-most fantasy points per game.

Williams is a strong bet to find the end zone this week. In his one game against the Giants last season, he finished as RB4 that week, rushing for 97 yards and one touchdown on 18 carries while reeling in six of seven targets for 33 yards. Williams is a must-start as a staple in one of the league's top offenses.

The Browns' second-year back has some long-term upside, but he gets a horrible matchup in Week 1 against the Jaguars defense that allowed the third-fewest fantasy points per game and the fewest rushing yards to opposing backs last season. Cleveland is a 7.5-point underdog, which suggests they may be forced to abandon the run if they go down early.

This will be Judkins' first game back since suffering a significant injury: a fractured fibula and dislocated right ankle in December. As a large road underdog, it's likely backup running back Dylan Sampson gets more usage than expected as Judkins is eased into action.

Lloyd has catapulted up fantasy rankings and draft boards since Josh Jacobs was placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Green Bay hits the road in Week 1 for a tough divisional matchup with the Vikings, who allowed the tenth-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing running backs a season ago.

Green Bay added Kaleb Johnson and has Chris Brooks available to take meaningful snaps as well. A report Tuesday, Sept. 8 indicated the Packers could deploy a committee to start the season, creating a legitimate threat to Lloyd's workload. Lloyd has played only one regular-season game, totaling six carries for 15 yards, and hasn't played an NFL regular-season snap since 2024. Lloyd has no strong track record to trust in Week 1.

The Commanders' second-year back is trending towards becoming a touchdown-dependent option for fantasy managers. With Rachaad White signing in Washington in the offseason, Croskey-Merritt will likely not be on the field during obvious passing situations, so there isn't a strong three-down role until proven otherwise.

Philadelphia finished last season as a respectable run defense, and with a healthy Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis, they pose a challenge for the Commanders' meager offensive line. Croskey-Merritt had also missed some practice time over the last few weeks with a lower-body issue, adding to the chance he splits more work than expected. There's some long-term intrigue if the Commanders can play from ahead, but Croskey-Merritt can be left on the bench in Week 1.

Lemon was the Eagles' No. 20 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. The rookie wideout did not have the most impressive of preseason showings: three receptions for three yards and a dropped pass leading to an interception against the Bengals in the Eagles' final exhibition game of the year. Prior to that, he missed time at training camp with a hamstring injury.

But preseason performance alone should not be a reason to panic – let Ja'Marr Chase's struggles in his rookie preseason be a reminder of that. Lemon is slotting in next to the Eagles' projected lead wideout, DeVonta Smith, and is coming off of an outstanding final year in college. His Week 1 matchup against the Commanders is favorable, too. Washington allowed the second-most expected points added (EPA) on passing plays in 2025, and the team did not do enough to improve its pass defense in a convincing way this offseason.

Downs had a down year – no pun intended – in 2025 but appears set for a return to form in 2026. With Michael Pittman Jr. gone to the Steelers, Downs could see a boost in his target share. That's true especially early in the season, as Pittman's projected replacement – Keenan Allen – was a late free agent signing and could need more time to integrate into the Colts' offense.

Baltimore got off to a very slow start last year as its defense struggled to stop opponents' passing attacks. Even by the end of the year, the Ravens had allowed the second-most passing yards per game behind only the Cowboys. Downs (calf) and Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (Achilles) are both on track to play Week 1. They could have a real opportunity to take advantage of Baltimore's shaky passing defense, which could see another slow start as it adjusts to new head coach Jesse Minter's system.

Johnston's 2025 season was a career year for him with 735 receiving yards and eight touchdowns on 51 catches. In 2026, he has even less competition for targets with veteran Keenan Allen departing for Indianapolis in the offseason. Ladd McConkey likely steps back into the Chargers' lead receiver role after finishing second on the team in catches in 2025, but Johnston is right there behind him in the No. 2 role.

Johnston is almost a no-brainer to start against the Cardinals – a team that ranked dead last in success rate allowed on dropbacks in 2025. Even with McConkey around to haul in most of the targets, Johnston should see plenty of looks of his own in his debut in the Chargers' new-look offense, coordinated by new OC Mike McDaniel.

Rice isn't expected to face NFL discipline after spending 30 days in jail this offseason for a violation of his probation. That is not why he should be considered for a bench spot in Week 1.

More relevant is his opponent and the quarterback situation he faces in Week 1. The Broncos boasted one of the best defenses in football last year – particularly against the pass, where they allowed the lowest success rate (38.5%) on dropbacks of any defense. Making things more difficult is for Rice is the fact he likely will be facing off against 2024 Defensive Player of the Year Patrick Surtain II on most of his routes. On top of that, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is making his first start back from a torn ACL and LCL he suffered last December. With Mahomes potentially rusty and the Chiefs emphasizing their run game with the signing of reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker, Rice might not have a productive first week in 2026.

Moore may be the Bills' new de facto No. 1 wide receiver after his arrival in Buffalo via trade this offseason, but that has not meant much in the post-Stefon Diggs era. In 2025, the Bills' leading receiver, Khalil Shakir, finished with just 719 yards and four touchdowns. That was after a 2024 season in which the leading receiver (Shakir again) had 821 yards and four touchdowns.

Buffalo's more "spread-the-wealth" approach to receiving output that began in 2024 correlated directly with three things: Diggs' departure from the team, Joe Brady's first year as full-time Bills OC and an uptick in rushing play percentage. In 2026, Brady is now the Bills' head coach but will still call plays for the offense.

As if those factors weren't bad enough indicators for Moore's Bills debut, he also has to make it in Houston. The Texans were the league's best team at limiting EPA and the second-best at limiting opponents' success rate on dropbacks. Essentially all of Houston's defensive core is back: Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter, Derek Stingley Jr. Plus, the Texans added safety Reed Blankenship. Moore's first matchup of 2026 does him no favors from a fantasy outlook perspective.

The Saints offense hasn't been as explosive since Drew Brees walked out the door, but fireworks may return in 2026. In the 11 games played with Tyler Shough in 2025, Johnson excelled, posting 11.5 fantasy points per game. He ultimately finished third among all tight ends in the NFL with 889 receiving yards.

Johnson posted career-highs in targets (102), receptions (77) and yards (889) a season ago. There's little target competition outside of Chris Olave, as rookie Jordyn Tyson remains sidelined with a hamstring injury. The Saints are expected to trail in this game which implies a passing game script. Start Johnson against the shaky Lions secondary in a game that has the second-highest total of Week 1 (49.5).

Until proven otherwise, target the Bengals with the tight end they are facing.

Cincinnati allowed the most receptions to opposing tight ends in 2024 and followed that up with an historically bad 2025, allowing the most receptions again and a staggering 17.45 fantasy points per game to the position. Otton isn't a set-it-and-forget-it for most fantasy managers, but he is the top streamer of Week 1. For squads who plan to taxi a tight end off waivers most weeks, Otton should be your target this week.

The Buccaneers open the season on the road against the Bengals in what projects to be the highest-scoring game of the week. With Emeka Egbuka and Jalen McMillan dealing with injuries, Baker Mayfield will likely lean on Chris Godwin and Otton in order to keep pace with the high-powered Bengals offense.

With A.J. Brown out of town, Goedert has an opportunity to be the second option in Philadelphia's offense behind DeVonta Smith. Goedert clearly has the trust of Jalen Hurts: he accounted for 40.9% of the team's targets inside the 10-yard line, which resulted in a career-high 11 TDs in 2025, and there's little reason to believe that number takes a significant dip in 2026 with Brown's 120 vacated targets. Goedert's targets per route when A.J. Brown was on the field was 18.8% over the last two seasons, and that number jumped to 27.1% when Brown was off the field.

The 31-year-old maintains his every-down role in 2026. Rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon will eventually pose a threat to Goedert's usage, but early on, the vet should be started with confidence. Philadelphia hosts the Commanders who surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends in 2025.

The Giants host the Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football," and Likely should be a key cog for "Big Blue." The 25-year-old is expected to be a focal point in the passing game after following head coach John Harbaugh from Baltimore and signing a $40 million contract. He was stuck behind Mark Andrews on the depth chart with the Ravens but in 10 games without Andrews throughout his first four NFL seasons, he scored seven touchdowns.

The Cowboys allowed the second-most points in 2024, then allowed the most in 2025, yielding a league-high 60 touchdowns. They made sweeping personnel changes across the defense during the offseason but also have a first-time defensive coordinator.

Star wide receiver Malik Nabers' health remains in question and plenty of focus is on the return of Odell Beckham Jr. Likely is one of the most overlooked tight ends in Week 1 and has breakout potential. Start him with confidence.

Kraft would be ranked inside the top five at the position if we knew he had a clean bill of health. After an early season breakout during which he posted 700 yards and 7 touchdowns, he tore his ACL in November. He's on track to play in Week 1 when Green Bay plays Minnesota on the road but recent comments suggest he will be eased back into action.

Romeo Doubs left in free agency, vacating a team-high 83 targets, opening up Kraft as an elite option when healthy. Green Bay signed Jonnu Smith, which could signal that Kraft could be on a snap count. The Brian Flores-coached Vikings defense allowed the sixth-fewest fantasy points to tight ends in 2025. Kraft has the potential to anchor your lineup as the season progresses but proceed with caution this week.

The Buffalo Bills hit the road in Week 1 and open the season against the NFL's No. 1 defense. It's unlikely Kincaid will make a significant mark in this matchup against the Texans. He will continue to split work with Dawson Knox while competing with D.J. Moore for targets.

Kincaid is a breakout candidate in 2026 but temper expectations in Week 1.

title: Which Aggies landed on NFL IR, PUP and practice squads?
description: Texas A&M has several players on NFL injured reserve, PUP and practice squads entering the 2026 season.
fullText:
The NFL season is underway, and while several Texas A&M football players earned spots on active rosters, a few are beginning the year on injured reserve or a practice squad. Some will miss the entire season, others could return in a few weeks, and the practice-squad players could receive a call-up as early as Sunday. NFL teams are always finding creative ways to manage their rosters.

Starting with the most unfortunate news, offensive lineman Chase Bisontis and edge rusher Nic Scourton will both miss the entire season with knee injuries. Arizona's second-round rookie Bisontis tore his MCL during the preseason. Scourton tore his ACL on Carolina's opening day of training camp after recording five sacks as a rookie.

title: Countdown to Kickoff: Spencer Rattler is the Saints Player of Day 2
description: Spencer Rattler goes into his third NFL season, now as the New Orleans Saints backup QB behind Tyler Shough. He's our Saints Player of the Day.
fullText:
Friday means a mere two days before the New Orleans Saints' 2026 regular season opener. The Saints will play at the Detroit Lions to start off their year on Sunday, Sept. 13. Quarterback Spencer Rattler wears No. 2 for New Orleans as he enters his third season. Rattler is our most recent Saints Player of the Day feature.

Name (age): Spencer Rattler (25)

Height, weight: 6-foot, 211 pounds

College: South Carolina Gamecocks

Drafted: Round 5, 150 overall in 2024

2026 salary cap hit: $1.16 million

A five-star prospect from Pinnacle High School, Rattler was a prominent national recruit who decided on the Oklahoma Sooners. He played sparingly as a true freshman in 2019 before winning the starting job the following year. Rattler led the Big 12 in completion percentage (67.5%), passing yards (3,031) and touchdowns (28) while guiding the Sooners to a 9-2 mark and earning 1st Team All-Big 12 honors. Entering 2021 as a Heisman Trophy favorite, Rattler was statistically solid but uneven play led to him getting benched in favor of Caleb Williams. He'd transfer to South Carolina at the season's conclusion.

Rattler quarterbacked the Gamecocks for his final two years of eligibility, leading them to a 13-12 overall mark. In those two seasons, he threw for 6,212 yards with 37 touchdowns, 20 interceptions, and a 67.5% completion percentage. Rattler's collegiate career ended with a 68.5% completion rate, 10,807 passing yards, 77 touchdowns, and 32 interceptions.

After six quarterbacks were picked in the first round of the 2024 NFL draft, their wasn't another signal caller chosen until the Saints grabbed Rattler in Round 5 with the 150th overall selection. He was expected to learn and develop behind starter Derek Carr for his first season. That all changed when Carr went down with an injury in Week 5. Rattler got his first career start in Week 6 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, playing well in spurts during a blowout loss. He'd start the next two games with worsening results until getting benched for Jake Haener against the Chargers. Carr returned the following week, but lasted just five games before going down again with a season-ending injury.

After Carr's second injury, the Saints turned to Haener to start against Washington. That experiment lasted only a half, as Rattler took over and played arguably his best game of the year. Those results didn't carry over, as Rattler started the year's last three games but really only played reasonably well in a season finale rematch against Tampa Bay. An albeit injury-depleted Saints team lost all seven of Rattler's game appearances, averaging just 13.3 points in the process. Rattler completed 57% of his throws for 1,317 yards with 4 touchdowns and 5 interceptions while taking 22 sacks.

Under new head coach Kellen Moore and an entirely new coaching staff in 2025, Rattler competed with second-round rookie draft choice Tyler Shough for the starting job in preseason. It was an even competition, but Rattler was given the opportunity to start the year. That lasted eight games before the Saints turned to Shough to start the remaining nine contests. Under Rattler, New Orleans averaged a meager 15.1 points per outing with Rattler averaging 198.3 passing yards per game and an abysmal 6.2 per attempt.

Spencer Rattler held off Zach Wilson for the backup job during the 2026 offseason. However, neither showed little to inspire confidence if they have to step in for Shough. Given his experience in the system, Rattler should be the favorite to back up Shough this season.

title: ‘Drowning myself’: Puka Nacua opens up about struggles with alcohol
description: The Los Angeles Rams, the heavy Super Bowl favorites entering the season, opened the year in the NFL’s first-ever game in Melbourne, Australia, against the San Francisco 49ers. The majority of the attention the Rams have gotten this offseason has been centered on the defensive line, which was bolstered by the acquisition of the NFL’s…
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams, the heavy Super Bowl favorites entering the season, opened the year in the NFL's first-ever game in Melbourne, Australia, against the San Francisco 49ers. The majority of the attention the Rams have gotten this offseason has been centered on the defensive line, which was bolstered by the acquisition of the NFL's single-season sack record holder Myles Garrett and the return of Aaron Donald from retirement.

However, Los Angeles also has one of the most potent offenses in the league, with reigning league MVP Matthew Stafford passing to two of the best wide receivers in the league, Davante Adams and Puka Nacua. Unfortunately for Nacua, he's been caught up in some off-the-field trouble recently.

Ahead of kickoff on Thursday, Nacua sat down with Netflix's Elle Duncan and spoke candidly about his struggles wth alcohol.

"I think I learned that I'm very avoidant of conflict, which is very interesting due to the football nature of… I would like to say I play very physical, just avoidant of the things that I know were causing me stress," Nacua told Duncan.

"Just, I think some of the change in lifestyle that came up to me, becoming a public figure, the stress of performing at a high level," he responded after being asked what was causing him stress. "And then I recently became a father. My son is 10 months old. And navigating that co-parenting relationship with his mother, I would kind of isolate myself to feel like the weight of all the issues and things that I have was stuck on my shoulders, and not being willing to ask for help. I was never one to share my fears and my worries. I was always Finding different ways to escape, I guess, from that tension or that stress."

Puka Nacua opened up about turning to alcohol to cope with the pressures of stardom.

“I was always finding different ways to escape… alcohol was definitely a thing for me.”

Now, the #Rams WR says he wants to become someone his son can be proud of.

(via @NetflixSports) pic.twitter.com/VToMvRw7Ra

— Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) September 10, 2026

"I think one, alcohol was definitely a thing for me," he added about how he looked to escape, "just kind of drowning myself so that the issues and the stress that I was feeling never had the opportunity to be addressed. But right when I entered the rehabilitation center, I was able to have open and honest conversations."

"As it sits right now, at 25 years old, with your whole life in front of you, what are you most looking forward to about who you're becoming?" Duncan asked.

"I'm looking forward most to, um, becoming a person that I think my son will be proud of."

Nacua led the NFL in first downs a season ago with 80 of them. If he can stay focused and out of trouble, there's nothing stopping him from having an offensive player of the year caliber campaign this season.

title: 'It's NFL everywhere' - American football fever hits Melbourne
description: The LA Rams will face the San Francisco 49ers in the first regular season American football game to be played Down Under.
fullText:
An oval ball, in September, in Melbourne usually means just one thing - the business end of the Australian rules football (AFL) season.

But on Friday, at the unsportingly early time of 7am, 100,000 people will begin filing into the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) for a very un-Australian sporting spectacle - American football.

The LA Rams take on the San Francisco 49ers in their opening National Football League (NFL) fixture, the first time the country has hosted a meaningful, non-exhibition regular season game.

The match sold out months ago, with more than half the crowd expected to be people living outside the state of Victoria. On the official ticket resale site, a restricted view seat is priced at more than A$650 (£350/US$470).

"Walking down the street, it's AFL finals week and you wouldn't even know," says Thomas McMillan, host of the NFL podcast Any Given Sunday Australia.

"It's all NFL everywhere. There are bars that are nothing but 49ers bars or Rams bars. We have a Ram Tram getting around the district. When you're in Melbourne and AFL isn't visible, it shows how big this is at the moment."

Kickoff at 10.35am local time on Friday may not be typical for local fans, but meets the demands of prime time US television schedules and their advertisers.

The league held its first international match in 2007, and over the past two decades the overseas matches have become a long-term strategy to attract supporters and their dollars.

Nine games outside the US are scheduled for the upcoming season, including three in London. But Melbourne is the furthest that players and US-based fans will have to travel.

"Obviously there are question marks when you hear you are playing in Australia," 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey told a press conference this week.

"But it has been so cool… the food's incredible, the coffee's great."

That caffeine reference was perhaps as much to the time zone, as nod to the city's famous café culture.

Melbourne is a mind-warping 17 hours ahead of California where both teams are based, and much of the pre-match attention has been on the two teams and their contrasting approaches to trying to "beat" the jet lag.

For the 49ers, who arrived late last week, their players have had time to get over the long journey, adjust to the time zone, acclimatise and practice at a nearby stadium.

Controversially, the LA Rams are taking things to the other extreme, planning to arrive on Thursday morning local time on a charted Qantas A380 superjumbo, play on Friday, and get back to the US west coast shortly afterwards, in theory to prepare for their next match with minimum disruption to the player's body clocks.

"Definitely it's a gamble," says McMillan. "If they don't quite get things right after the 16-hour flight, you still might have that jet lag, even though you're trying to avoid it."

"And not everyone can sleep on planes," says his co-host Danny Webb. "Whether you're in first class, business class, whatever it is, you're still on a plane."

"And", adds McMillan: "And they're six foot six most of them, so it's going to be even tighter seats".

Despite it technically being a "home" game for the Rams, who bid for NFL marketing rights in Australia under the leagues Global Markets programme, this all means it is the San Francisco 49ers that have more of a presence around Melbourne this week.

And while most practice sessions have been behind closed doors, there have been player appearances at a rally for fans and an AFL match, while ex-stars turned up at that most Australian of traditions, the weekly fundraising "sausage sizzle" at the country's most high-profile hardware chain.

American sports journalist Dontay Atkinson predicts this fan engagement will be reflected inside the stadium and that the MCG will be "heavily red" (the 49ers colour), accusing the Rams of doing "exactly jack squat to sell the NFL brand or connect with Australians".

Writing on X he added: "Fly in, fly out, no contact. I'm sure the Aussies feel great about that snub."

McMillan says he can understand the approach by the Rams, who are seen as contenders for the 2027 Superbowl.

"They're looking at this as a game they need to win," he says.

"We do feel a bit snubbed, and feel the 49ers are doing the right thing,

"But it is their job, so that's where the Rams coaching staff has gone 'nah, we're taking this approach'.

"I just worry that they have missed the boat of ingraining themselves as the Australian team. It leaves it open for others, and the 49ers have really jumped on that."

The LA Rams insist there has been no snub, though speaking to the BBC, the club's Head of International Stephanie Cheng dodged the question of whether she would have preferred her players to have been in town this week.

"It's really a culmination of more than four years of work," she said. "It's not just about game week. We have long term rights."

Cheng says the Rams are the only NFL team with a membership programme for Australian fans, and that it has sent coaches into schools and communities to promote "flag football" – the non-contact version of the sport which will feature in the LA 2028 Olympics.

She also points to regular earlier visits by star players including running back Kyren Williams in March. This week its cheerleaders have visited US military bases in Australia before coming to Melbourne, and the franchise has installed a 22-yard floating football field on Melbourne's Yarra River serving as a fan zone.

"From day one, when we've come to Australia, there's been incredible enthusiasm," Cheng said.

While no Australian players will be on the field on Friday, there are dozens playing US college football and a handful in the NFL.

Most are punters, kicking specialists tapped up after showing their prowess playing AFL or rugby league.

But it is the success of Jordan Mailata, an offensive left tackle with the Philadelphia Eagles, who in 2025 became the first Australian to play in, and win, a Superbowl that was a "major turning point in Australia's fandom of the NFL " says Webb.

"Seeing an Australian in what we'd called a skilled position and then winning a Superbowl. It doesn't get better than that".

Friday's game is the first of three matches in Melbourne to be held over four years, under a contract between the NFL and the state of Victoria.

The league's preference, says Gerrit Meier, managing director and head of NFL International, is to have annual games in Australia similar, to the way the game has grown in the UK.

"We're working off the hypothesis that we need to make a commitment to a market," he told Reuters.

And while many US-based supporters are not fans of the international fixtures, these games are here to stay, says Webb, and the hype and the sell-out crowd in Australia augurs well for it to become a long-term fixture,

"I had mates four years ago asking why are you doing an NFL podcast? It's not a big sport here," he said.

"And now every single one of those mates are asking me for tickets for the game."

title: Why is there an NFL game in Australia?
description: The NFL has so far played regular-season games in seven international countries but this week's trip to Australia represents a new frontier for the USA's biggest sports league.
fullText:
The NFL has so far played regular-season games in seven international countries but this week's trip to Australia represents a new frontier.

It is the NFL's first game in the Asia-Pacific region, with the USA's biggest sports league making its longest-ever road trip for the first of a record nine international games in 2026.

It will take place about 10,000 miles from the NFL's New York headquarters, in front of about 100,000 fans at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground.

That means the Los Angeles Rams will 'host' the San Francisco 49ers on a more open oval field on Friday (01:35 BST).

But when NFL commissioner Roger Goodell visited the MCG for the first time in April, he said the historic arena "speaks to you", and it says "this is the right place to be".

American football is coming to Australia - can it succeed?

Live NFL games have been broadcast in Australia since 1995 and a pre-season exhibition game was held in Sydney in 1999.

Local interest has soared since 2022, though, when the NFL made the global growth of American football a strategic priority.

The league pivoted away from a potential overseas franchise to playing more games internationally. It has invested in new markets before deciding whether to take a game there, holding year-round events to build the fanbase.

Australian players Jordan Mailata (Philadelphia) and Michael Dickson (Seattle) have also captured the imagination down under, playing for the past two Super Bowl winners.

According to the league, the number of fans in Australia has nearly doubled since 2022 to 8.8 million - almost one in three of the country's entire population.

That includes those flooding to one of the world's fastest-growing sports, flag football - the non-contact version of American football.

The NFL played a big part in flag being approved for its Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028 and has expanded the sport from 10 schools in Australia to more than 500.

Now it aims to help flag football secure a spot at Brisbane 2032, with NFL executive Peter O'Reilly acknowledging that is a key reason for playing in Australia.

Being a sports-mad country, Australia was always on the NFL's radar, and after testing long-distance logistics with trips to Brazil in 2024 and 2025, the league felt ready to head down under.

Sydney and Perth were in the running but Melbourne is regarded as the nation's sports capital and the MCG is the biggest stadium in the southern hemisphere.

A deal was announced in February 2025, during Super Bowl week, and while some fans expressed anger at ticket prices when they went on sale in April 2026, they sold out in minutes.

The state of Victoria is reportedly paying up to A$15m, external (£8m) for the right to host the game but expects one of the state's biggest returns. Dublin enjoyed a tenfold return on its investment to stage its first NFL game last September.

Almost 50% of the MCG tickets were bought by fans outside Victoria or overseas, so about 50,000 fans will visit Melbourne this week.

'The G' is also right next to Melbourne Park, home of tennis' Australian Open, an ideal venue for a three-day fan festival, which began with a watch party for last night's season opener.

The NFL picked this year's Super Bowl week to announce that the 49ers will be the Rams' opponents in Melbourne, which created a buzz in Australia and California.

Not only are the Rams and 49ers regular Super Bowl contenders but they are also divisional rivals in the ultra-competitive NFC West. In addition, there is heaps of hype around the Rams.

With this season's Super Bowl being held in LA, they have gone all-in to reach the big game. First they traded for defensive stars Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie, which cemented them as championship favourites.

Then three-time defensive player of the year Aaron Donald returned from retirement and although the 35-year-old has not travelled to Australia, Garrett and McDuffie will both make their Rams debut at the MCG.

Fred Warner, Nick Bosa and George Kittle are set to return from injury for the 49ers, with Mike Evans making his debut.

The game will be broadcast live on Netflix, reaching more than 200 countries, while the Jonas Brothers will perform a half-time show.

California is 17 hours behind Melbourne and the flight takes about 16 hours. The previous longest for a regular-season game was about 12 hours to Sao Paulo, Brazil.

Yet the two teams have taken a completely different approach. The 49ers arrived in Melbourne last Friday while the Rams arrived the day before the game - just as they did for last year's comfortable win at Wembley over the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The huge time difference means that the game kicks off at 10:35 on Friday in Melbourne - which is Thursday evening in the United States: 17:35 on the west coast, 20:35 on the east.

While a morning start (local time) is virtually unheard of in the NFL, it's perfectly normal for fans used to watching cricket at the MCG.

The long flights and early start have thrown each teams' regular routine out of kilter. San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan admitted he was struggling to remember what day it was.

But having the game in week one gives each team the best chance to cope with the travel demands, rather than playing it later in the season.

The NFL has committed to playing one more game in Melbourne in the next three years, with the possibility of another.

What sets Australia apart from other countries hosting international games is that ball-carrying sports are the most popular down under.

All seven Australians in the NFL converted from rugby, basketball or Australian rules football, and Australia has a huge pool of similar athletes with transferable skills.

The NFL has pledged to provide flag football kits to every school in Australia and opened an academy on the Gold Coast as it aims to tap into that talent, which could produce an international pipeline of players targeting the Olympics and the NFL.

title: Champions Seahawks beat Patriots in season opener
description: Defending champions the Seattle Seahawks come from behind to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 in the opening game of the NFL season.
fullText:
Defending champions the Seattle Seahawks came from behind to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 in the opening game of the NFL season.

For the first time in 10 years the season began with a rematch of the Super Bowl, in which the Patriots were dominated by a Seahawks defence known as 'the Dark Side'.

Again they stepped up after Seattle lost quarterback Sam Darnold to a hip injury in the game's opening drive, claiming three interceptions in the final quarter at Lumen Field.

The Patriots went into a 10-0 lead, with rookie tight end Eli Raridon scoring the first touchdown of the season in the second quarter.

Back-up quarterback Drew Lock got the Seattle offence going late in the third quarter, with Jason Myers cutting the gap with a field goal.

Seahawks cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett claimed his first career interception at the start of the fourth quarter, after a Drake Maye pass was deflected by rookie Rodney Thomas.

On the next possession Lock found wide reciever Jaxon Smith-Njigba in space and last season's offensive player of the year charged through the Patriots defence for a 45-yard touchdown.

Julian Love then picked off Patriots quarterback Maye, giving Myers the chance to edge the Seahawks in front with a 26-yard field goal.

New England were well within field-goal range with 21 seconds remaining, but chose to go for the win rather than settle for overtime, and the move backfired as Maye's hopeful pass towards Mack Hollins was intercepted by Josh Jobe in the endzone.

The only game in which Maye threw multiple interceptions last season was the Super Bowl, and he was picked off on the Patriots' final three possessions in the season opener.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said: "You can't throw three interceptions. Drake knows that."

Maye said his final interception was "unacceptable", adding: "We could have sent it to overtime at the worst, and the only thing I could do was turn the ball over."

Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald said initial tests showed Darnold had not fractured a hip.

Week one continues with the NFL's first regular-season game in Australia. The Los Angeles Rams meet the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne on Thursday (01:35 BST, Friday).

fullText:
(WFRV) -- Every year, the NFL releases an updated playbook with newly worded and changed rules, much to the chagrin and controversy of avid football watchers.

The nearly 100-page playbook includes four substantive rule changes from its current edition to last year's, two of which involve kickoffs.

The first rule change concerns kickoff formations. Rule 6-1-3 gives the receiving team more flexibility in designing return formations, so only five players must be on the restraining line when there are nine players in the setup zone. Previously, six were required. Now, only six are required if there are more than nine players.

The second rule change concerns kickoffs at the fifty-yard line. To prevent a situation where accepting a touchback off a 50-yard-line kickoff is worse than kicking it out of bounds, rule 6-1-5 makes it so that touchbacks from that kickoff placement are now placed at the 20-yard line, versus the 35-yard line like it used to be.

Still keeping with the kicking theme, the third rule drastically changes the concept of onside kicks. While only a trailing team could do onside kicks, Rule 6-1-6 now lets any team declare an onside kick at any point in the game.

The final drastic rule change concerns the power league officials have. Rule 19-2 allows league officials to intervene on a flagrant football or non-football act that wasn't called on the field. Previously, league officials could only help after a flagrant foul had already been called.

The rule states that the decision to intervene must be based on available video, and that the intervention must happen before the next play begins.

title: NFL Kickoff 2026: Patriots lead Seahawks 7-0 at halftime
description: The Patriots lead the Seahawks 7-0 at halftime, but Seattle has a bigger concern moving forward.
fullText:
The Patriots lead the Seahawks 7-0 at halftime, but Seattle has a bigger concern moving forward.

Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold exited the game after the first series with a hip injury. He appeared to suffer it when he was sacked by Dre'Mont Jones on third down, which brought up a punt.

Darnold limped to the sideline before he was eventually examined in the medical tent. He then limped off the field up to the locker room for further evaluation.

Just before halftime, the Seahawks ruled him out.

Backup Drew Lock played the rest of the first half for Seattle. So far, he's completed 6-of-8 passes for 51 yards. But the Seahawks have also struggled to move the ball, registering six first downs.

On the other side, Drake Maye has been a lot more effective than he was against Seattle's defense in Super Bowl LX back in February. He's gotten off some quick passes and used his legs effectively to scramble. Though Maye's most productive pass was one that wasn't even completed — as newcomer A.J. Brown drew a defensive pass interference penalty that put the Patriots at Seattle's 2-yard line.

On the next play, Maye tossed a 2-yard touchdown to rookie tight end Eli Rairdon for the NFL's first touchdown of 2026.

Maye finished the first half 10-of-12 for 66 yards with a touchdown.

The Patriots have 10 first downs, 130 yards, and are 3-of-7 on third down.

Seattle has 120 yards and is 1-of-6 on third down. They may want to have a heavy dose of rookie Jadarian Price in the second half, who has 42 yards on his six carries in his debut.

The Patriots will receive the second-half kickoff.

title: First tush push of NFL season draws penalty, spoils would-be drive-saving dart from backup Seahawks QB Drew Lock
description: The infamous tush push appears to continue to be a point of emphasis for NFL officials.
fullText:
With Sam Darnold sidelined, Drew Lock threw what looked like a drive-saving downfield dart for the Seattle Seahawks as they sought their first score of the new NFL season against the New England Patriots Wednesday night.

But a borderline penalty on a failed tush push mitigated the effort, and the Seahawks came away from the drive without any points. The penalty also set the tone for what appears to remain a point of emphasis for NFL officiating.

The sequence started on third-and-22 at Seattle's 33-yard line. With Darnold out of the game with a hip injury sustained on the first drive, Lock dropped back on the third-and-long snap and looked deep dowfield.

He found Jaxon Smith-Njigba just short of the sticks with a laser between multiple Patriots defenders.

Drew Lock and JSN with a big gain on 3rd and 22.

NEvsSEA on NBC/Peacock
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Bg1bAKodHD

This set up and obvious go-for-it situation on fourth-and-goal near midfield with a 7-0 deficit late in the second quarter.

Go for it, the Seahawks did, with their version of the tush push made infamous by the Philadelphia Eagles. With their iteration, they lined up 251-pound tight end AJ Barner under center in a tight bunch formation. They appeared to get the first down in Patriots territory with a late push on the play.

But a whistle blew. And officials called an offside penalty.

This offside was called on the offense. Officials say right guard Anthony Bradford lined up over the line of scrimmage.

Here's another look. It's tough to tell from NBC's overhead angle if officials got the call right.

Refs flagged the Seahawks offensive line offsides on this successful tush push. Seahawks now forced to punt pic.twitter.com/JjXTrgEsf5

Regardless, the result of the play was a five-yard penalty on Seattle, which resulted in another Seahawks punt, their fourth of the half.

They went into halftime without any points and a 7-0 deficit and Darnold ruled out for the rest of the game.
